correctness.rationale: For each \(n\ge4\), the norm upper bound is attained by positive singular vectors at the unique strictly-convex envelope optimizer; the norm-one plateau is characterized by the top singular subspace. The Schur-complement computation about the multiple unit singular value gives \(s_n(t)=1+q_nt+a_nt^2/2+O(t^3)\) with \(a_n=(n+2)\sin^2(\pi/n)/n\). Inverting its derivative proves the exact quadratic coefficient. The endpoint \(q=1\) follows from the standard numerical radius. Finite tests do not stand in for proof.

value.rationale: The finite truncated shift is a natural model contraction for spectral-set questions. The exact all-order onset at \(q_n=\cos(\pi/n)\) and the nonzero explicit quadratic curvature quantify the transition from full operator-norm saturation to constrained decay. The dimensional coefficient and full singular-norm variational profile are motivated structural invariants, not a normalization, isolated parameter substitution, or table recomputation.
